name: @propertyiq/video-template
description: Remotion video template for PropertyIQ YouTube channel
//narration-dist-exports: The two ./dist/narration/* entries are explicit rather than covered by the ./dist/* wildcard, and that is load-bearing. The backend compiles with moduleResolution:node, which predates `exports`, so it must import by dist path — but Node DOES honour `exports` at runtime, and a wildcard target matches LITERALLY with no extension inference, so an extensionless specifier resolves to a file that does not exist. Neither tsc nor jest catches this (jest uses node-style resolution and ignores `exports` entirely); the only symptom is the backend failing to boot with MODULE_NOT_FOUND. NOTE comment keys must live here at the top level — a `//`-prefixed key inside `exports` makes Node reject the whole package with ERR_INVALID_PACKAGE_CONFIG.
//exports: The manifest is read by three consumers — the renderer, the create-run contract, and the admin wizard — but only the first lives in this package, so the catalogue needs a real entry point. It sits on its own subpath rather than the package root because the root (src/index.ts) is Remotion's entry: importing it calls registerRoot() and drags in the whole composition tree, React and Mapbox included. ./formats is pure data and constants, safe in a Next.js bundle. NOTE the ./dist/* wildcard is load-bearing: an exports map is a whitelist, and the backend renderer resolves ./dist/cli/render-cli.js by path. Dropping it silently breaks every video render.
//peerDependencies: React is a PEER, not a dependency. Declaring it as a dependency made npm install a nested copy that could never dedupe with the frontend's React, so importing a composition into Next.js loaded two Reacts at once ('Invalid hook call'). Remotion itself only requires >=16.8.0.
